function: Time-domain extrapolation of massive MIMO precoding matrices: transformer (TPN) predicts future-RB precoders from historical ones, CNN (CPSN) predicts one precoder, rate loss (pp. 1, 5-6).
system: Massive MIMO-OFDM downlink; BS 32-antenna UPA, user 4-antenna ULA, 28 GHz, 30 kHz subcarrier spacing; antenna sweeps 64 to 2; no RIS (Table I, p. 7; Figs. 10, 16).
method: Transformer encoder TPN (8 heads, 2 layers, d=256, causal mask) and CNN-based CPSN with structured pruning and fine-tuning; trained with a negative-rate loss from the true channel (pp. 5-7).
data_channel: CDL-C model cited to 3GPP TR 38.811 [36]: 28 GHz, 30 kHz spacing, 20 m/s; training and testing data generated from it (pp. 7, 12).
test_conditions: Train and test on CDL-C data (28 GHz, 20 m/s); sweeps of input antennas (retrained), sounding period, SNR and 2-4 users with EZF; no unseen channel scenario (pp. 7-11).
baselines: Zero-order holding (non-learned); TFNET [30], CNN-CNN and CNN-RNN (learned precoding-matrix predictors) (pp. 8-9).
metrics: Sum-rate gain (%) over zero-order holding, achievable rate, inference time, FLOPs (Figs. 9-19, Tables II-III, pp. 7-11).
complexity: FLOPs formulas for TPN (Eq. 23) and CPSN (Eqs. 24-25); CPSN 372,550 FLOPs at pruning ratio 0.1; TPN inference 6.31 ms (2.63 ms with KV cache) (pp. 6-10).
q1_support: p. 7: "We adopt the clustered delay line (CDL)-C model [36] to generate the channel"; p. 12: ref. [36] is "Study on New Radio (NR) To Support Non-terrestrial Networks, document TR 38.811, 3GPP, 2020".
q2_support: p. 8: "we decrease the antenna numbers of the input and train TPN to predict the precoding matrix of full antennas". The antenna, sounding-period, SNR and multi-user results (pp. 8-11) are sweeps or extensions of one CDL-C dataset (p. 7); the paper never states a model trained in one scenario and tested in another.
q3_support: p. 8: "We compare the performance of the proposed TPN and TFNET in [30]" and "the proposed TPN is better than the TFNET"; gains are "versus the zero-order holding method are 14.29%, 14.62%, 15.54%, and 15.27%" (non-learned). TFNET [30] is an earlier learned precoding predictor by the same authors.
q4_support: p. 7: "Totally, the FLOPs of the whole TPN is" Eq. (23), with Eqs. (24)-(25) for CPSN; p. 10: "when the pruning ratio is 0.1, the FLOPs is 372, 550"; p. 9: "The total inference time required to generate all four precoding matrices is 6.31 ms".
q5_support: p. 7: "We adopt the clustered delay line (CDL)-C model [36] to generate the channel". The data are generated by the authors from a channel model; the paper gives no code or data link, DOI, public dataset or measurements.
notes: Area 3 rather than 2: the network outputs the BS precoder, is trained with a rate loss (Eq. 21, p. 5; p. 10 'the loss function is the opposite number of the rate of B4') and is judged by sum-rate gain over zero-order holding; the alternative reading is channel prediction (area 2). q1: CDL-C is cited to 3GPP TR 38.811 (NTN study, ref. [36], p. 12) although the setup is terrestrial 28 GHz with a 32-antenna UPA; the reviewer should confirm it counts. q2: the closest cases are the multi-user test with EZF (p. 11, per-user precoders reused) and the input-antenna sweep, which trains TPN for each case (p. 8). Tables I-III are images (pp. 7-8) and were read from the page images. Table I lists a 32-antenna UPA while Figs. 10 and 16 sweep input antennas from 64 to 2.
